# A package is a program when its body renders a node, and a window is one
# such node rather than the thing asked for. A bar with no window -- a status
# line i3 reads off stdout -- builds: its body renders the host, which is a
# member of `root` like a window.
#
# This used to be refused, "a program declares at least one window", which
# the package body answered by holding no window.

sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 -o out app.sngl
exists out/model.go
grep 'func Encode' out/model.go

# A body that renders nothing is still no program, whatever it declares.
! sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 -o none nothing.sngl
stderr 'a program renders something at the root of a file'

-- app.sngl --
import build "sngl:build"
import gen "sngl:x/gen"
import go "sngl:language/go"

component block build.family

component text(full string) block

component bar(blocks ...component block) root

struct Entry {
    full string
}

#[go.native("fmt", "fmt.Print")]
func print(s string)

func encode(members list<Entry>) string {
    var parts list<string> = []
    for var e = members {
        parts.push(e.full)
    }
    return parts.join("|")
}

component block[go.language] {
    gen.emit(render=encode, @change(line) {
        print(line + "\n")
    })
}

component text[go.language] {
    gen.node(value=Entry{full=full})
}

var n = 0

bar {
    text(full="{n}")
}
-- nothing.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

component card ui.node {
    ui.text(value="hi")
}
